A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dataset, segmentation baseline and diffusion-model project, renamed from UniEM-3M/UniEM-Net to EM3M/UniAIMS. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including tables and rendered figures, and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation benchmarks, real-versus-synthetic training experiments, generative-model evaluations and dataset analyses, including Tables 2-4.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation and generation experiments and adds annotation-agreement measurements, external-dataset evaluations and supplementary performance analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use a Cellpose-inspired flow predictor with foreground probabilities and a SAM-pretrained ViT-Base backbone, alongside SDXL adaptation using LoRA and learned tokens. v2 newly explains size-model removal, LSJ augmentation and CUDA flow computation as adaptations of Cellpose; it does not establish that these replace a different procedure in v1. Renaming UniEM-Net to UniAIMS is not an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates segmentation within UniEM-3M. v2 adds zero-shot and fine-tuned evaluation on EMPS and the Okunev dataset, previously discussed only as prior datasets, substantially extending coverage to external transfer evaluation (Table 5). The central collection retains 5,091 images and 2,985,660 masks.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark expands from v1 Table 2 to v2 Table 3 by adding YOLO11-seg, SOLOv2, FastInst, MaskDINO and HoverNet. These are evaluated comparators, not merely new citations. v2's Cellpose comparator cites the same Cellpose-SAM work used in v1; its changed backbone and implementation should not be mistaken for an entirely new comparator.

E3.justification: Dense-subset reporting becomes full-dataset reporting for bottom-up methods. Baseline budgets change from 72 epochs to specified 60,000/180,000-iteration schedules, with revised learning-rate policies. Cellpose changes from ViT-Large to ViT-Base and is documented at 256×256 input resolution. v2 retains default detection limits rather than v1's increased limits. New protocols include the 300-image annotation audit, external transfer evaluation and PQ@90. These are reported protocol revisions, without independently establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative annotation-pipeline validation (Table 2), performance breakdowns by material, morphology and object size (Figure 8), acquisition-hardware analyses (Figure 10), and memory scaling with instance limits (Figure 12). Section 6 additionally tests stricter boundary agreement through PQ@90. The data-volume and synthetic-pretraining analyses already existed in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces statistical annotation-reliability reporting using Krippendorff's alpha from three independent annotators, plus boxplots of memory measurements collected over 1,000 training iterations. Neither version reports repeated-training seed counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for segmentation performance; these additions do not establish repeated independent training runs.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores are extensively replaced under revised settings, preventing direct same-setting performance comparisons. In the data-volume tables, the 30K-synthetic mAP/PQ row changes from 0.773/0.670 to 0.791/0.690, and mixed training changes from 0.807/0.705 to 0.809/0.707; real-data rows remain unchanged. v2 adds annotation, transfer and robustness results. The reported SEM share changes from 90.9% to 84.9%, while FID and Style scores remain identical.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theorems, proofs or substantive formal derivations. v2 Appendix 8 expands the explanation of existing Cellpose flows, scale normalization and reconstruction. The AP formula is retained; distinguishing it from COCO-style AP is clarification rather than a new mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The central dataset, generation and segmentation-benchmark contributions remain. v2 drops the generator's claimed privacy-preserving, full-distribution-surrogate role and presents UniAIMS more explicitly as an optimized Cellpose baseline. Release wording changes from a planned public subset to publicly available EM3M.

C2.justification: The new Open Problems section qualifies v1's strongly positive account with remaining crowding, boundary, contrast and scale failures, supported by PQ falling from 0.704 at IoU 0.5 to 0.340 at 0.9. v2 also acknowledges physically implausible attribute recombinations, explains the augmented-real FID reference, and introduces interpretations concerning external-benchmark saturation and memory bottlenecks.

D1.justification: v2 adds separate dataset, generator and demo access instructions, source proportions, exact sparse-split counts, an SDXL prompt template, and a codebase mapping in Table 7. It expands implementation disclosures concerning LSJ, CUDA flow computation and baseline-specific settings. The reported Aversa-source contribution changes from approximately 500 to 300 images. Conversely, v1's specific Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-o4-mini annotation-model identifiers are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of query-based segmentation, adds OmniScience and privacy/data-sharing literature, and explicitly positions UniAIMS as an implementation adaptation of Cellpose. The underlying materials-dataset gap and principal research lineage remain, making this a bounded expansion and refinement of positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark discussion and implementation/prediction appendices are extensively rewritten. Dataset construction moves before methodology, the flow explanation expands into dedicated appendix sections, and Open Problems becomes a separate section. Dataset/model terminology, authorship text and citation presentation also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with substantial resizing and relocation of displays. v2 adds annotation, transfer and codebase tables and subgroup, hardware and memory figures. The retained pretraining and t-SNE plots are merged into Figure 6; prediction grids are revised, generated examples expanded, and attribute charts redrawn.

improvement.justification: v1 describes expert annotation review without measuring its reliability; v2 supplies a 300-image independent-annotation audit and stagewise agreement results, addressing an important evidence gap for a dataset paper. Explicit failure conditions, clearer Cellpose attribution and fuller protocol documentation substantially strengthen credibility and interpretation. New reporting flaws temper the gain: the blanket zero-shot superiority claim conflicts with EMPS scores of 0.89 versus 0.92 in Table 5, and the revised 84.9% SEM figure contradicts retained 'over 90%' prose. These flaws do not outweigh the central validation improvements.
